headline: Pass‑through and burst signals are present but no laundering structure (cycle, layering, convergence or fan‑out) is detected; the activity is consistent with a legitimate travel‑agency partnership.

claims.text: Network signals show pass‑through (out/in ratio 1.23, 122 % of inflows left within 72 h) and burst (8 distinct counterparties in the busiest 24 h vs. 1.1 average) as suspicious; all structural signals (cycle, layered_transfers, convergence, interconnection, uniform_amounts, hubs) are context (0).

verdict.reason: Analyze_network lists pass_through and burst as suspicious with the quoted values; all structural signals (cycle, layered_transfers, convergence, interconnection, uniform_amounts, hubs) are context (0).

counter_evidence.text: No cycle detected – no ring of similar‑sized payments through non‑hub accounts returns to the subject.

verdict.reason: Cycle signal is context (0/3) with description “No ring…”, and query Q-df9ebae2c3 returns 0 rows.

counter_evidence.text: No layered transfers – none of the subject’s one‑off transfers is passed on (or funded) by another transfer within 72 h.

verdict.reason: Layered_transfers signal is context (0/3) stating none of the subject’s one‑off transfers are passed on or funded within 72 h.

counter_evidence.text: No convergence – no non‑hub account collects from or funds several of the subject’s counterparties.

verdict.reason: Convergence signal is context (0/3) stating no non‑hub account collects from or funds several of the subject’s counterparties.

would_change_my_mind: Evidence of a cycle returning funds to the subject account.
Layered transfers where outbound funds are quickly forwarded by counterparties within days.
Convergence of multiple counterparties onto a single downstream account.
A watchlist match on the subject itself.

sanctions_referral.reason: No strong watchlist match on the subject.

limitations: 11 counterparties at Institution B could not be screened by name because B’s governed view withholds names and dates of birth.
Investigation window limited to 10 days (1‑10 Sep 2022); longer‑term patterns are unknown.
Beneficial ownership of Institution B counterparties cannot be verified.
11 counterparties at Institution B could not be screened by name: B's governed view (inst_b.kyc_b_shared) withholds names and dates of birth.
narrative: Botella & Andrade Partners (ES, travel agency) moved $268.8 k inbound and $331.1 k outbound over 1‑10 Sep 2022 across five counterparties each, with a modest out‑to‑in ratio of 1.23 and a burst of eight distinct counterparties in a single day. Two‑hop tracing shows outbound funds dispersed to seven downstream accounts ($174.5 k) and inbound funds originating from a much larger upstream pool ($4.4 M), but no funds returned to the subject, no layered forwarding, and no convergence of counterparties onto a single account. Watchlist screening found no match for the subject; a single counterparty produced a name‑only hit with mismatched identifiers. Given the absence of any structural laundering pattern (cycle, layering, fan‑out, convergence) the activity is consistent with normal travel‑agency cash‑flow and is closed.
decision_basis: The model's conclusion and the measured structure agree.
